correctness.rationale: Directly conjugating the two specified traceless symmetric matrices gives the exact trial loss. Gaussian rotational symmetry produces a uniform unsigned angle, the best-of-L choice its minimum-order-statistic distribution. Exact integration yields E[L1]=2 epsilon; uniform comparison near the singular angular endpoint yields E[L2] ~ (16/pi^2) epsilon^2 log(1/epsilon); dominated convergence for L>=3 and integration by parts for L=3 yield the finite constants. Orthogonal minimization gives 2 epsilon^2. These analytic arguments establish all required quantifiers for 0<epsilon<1 and integer L>=1. The standalone verifier passes 2,100 rational identities and independent quadratures; finite computations are corroborative only.

The newly proved exact two-by-two law, matching one/two-trial lower rates and constants, and sharp three-trial witness are not stated or implied by the inspected tail upper bounds or by the differently scoped congruence and joint-eigenvalue papers. Equivalent specialized mathematical formulations outside inspected sources remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: A motivated numerical robustness question asks how many independent restarts are required to convert Gaussian high-probability near-diagonalization into constant-factor mean squared off-diagonal loss. The exact smallest-dimensional example proves a logarithmic loss at two trials and a finite optimal ratio at three, with sharp constants. It supplies a rigorous boundary/benchmark for an existing practical algorithm rather than a routine renaming of its known upper tail. The statement does not claim a broader solver complexity guarantee.
